Finance · design review changes F1, F3, F4 — and the F7 check

Decided in the design review (change list §2.6): F1 Star’s date picker (v1.018) for the Daily report’s calendar and Export’s dates · F3 History’s back link (v1.020) · F4 no icon on the phone ⋯ Today (v1.024) · F7 “after $X refunds” on Both (v1.022 / D3) — already built with F8, checked here. Each is drawn Now and After at PC 1280 × 800, tablet 820 × 1180 (touch), phone 390 × 844 (touch) and 320 wide. Amber outline = what changes. Brown text = a question or wording to confirm. F2, F5 and F6 are not drawn (F2 has its own mockup; F5–F6 change nothing on screen).

Daily report (approved D4): Star’s date picker for the day (F1, v1.018) — one question

What changes, whichever option

  • Today the calendar button opens the browser’s own date picker, which looks different on the desk PC, the iPad and a phone (it can’t be photographed, so the “Now” pictures show the button only). After: the same big month calendar Star’s dialogs use (DatePicker.jsx): Month and Year lists, Su–Sa, today outlined, the chosen day blue-tinted, days after today gray.
  • Picking a day opens that day’s report; picking today goes back to “today” (as now). Staff never see the calendar (unchanged).
  • Phones: the calendar opens in the page under the date row, edge to edge (the picker’s phone layout, v0.503); PC and tablet: a box under the field or button.
  • Wording to OK (invented): the calendar’s gray line “Days after today can’t be chosen.” (Star’s says “Past dates can’t be chosen.”). The same line is used in Export — one OK covers both.

The question: how does the calendar open?

  • Option A · the date itself is the picker — the bold day heading and the calendar button are replaced by the picker’s own field: a button with the date in words and a ⌄ (“Monday, October 26, 2026 ⌄”); a click opens the calendar under it.
    + Needs no change to the shared picker (its formatValue prop keeps today’s words per size: long on PC, “Mon, Oct 26, 2026” on tablet, “Mon, Oct 26” on phones), so Finance can build it now.
    − It changes the approved D4 row: the day is no longer a bold heading (it would stay a hidden heading for screen readers) and the calendar icon goes.
    − The field is as wide as its date, so the row moves as you change days: “Wednesday, September 30, 2026” is wider than “Monday, May 3, 2027”, which pushes ›, Today and History to the right on PC.
  • Option B · the calendar button opens the picker — the row stays exactly as today; the calendar button opens the same calendar under itself.
    + The approved D4 row stays exactly as it is: the bold day heading, the ‹ › arrows, the calendar icon.
    + A long date doesn’t widen anything new — the heading already sits where it does today.
    − Needs a new option in the shared DatePicker.jsx (open its calendar from another button, without its own field). That change goes through you and the Dashboard core session first, because Color Belt, Black Belt, Camps and new students are switching to the picker too; Finance’s F1 waits for it. (Prospects’ follow-up date, ProspectPanel.jsx ~258–270, probably needs the same option.)
  • Recommended: B — it keeps the approved screen unchanged and gives the same calendar, and the new option is likely needed by Prospects too, so the shared change pays twice. If Dashboard core can’t add it soon, A is a working fallback that needs nothing from anyone.

Sample: Worcester, Monday Oct 26, 2026 (the preview’s today is Wednesday Oct 28). Pictures are the real preview app with the change drawn on top; nothing in the app was changed.

Daily report, phone ⋯ menu (approved D14): “Today” loses its icon (F4, v1.024)

What changes

  • Only on phones, only for admins on an earlier day: the ⋯ sheet’s Today item drops its calendar-event icon (§2.4 “Go to today: no icon”, like the PC / tablet Today button and the Calendar’s Today).
  • Its place stays as a blank 16 px slot (NoIcon, menu-icon ev-noicon, as Color Belt and Camps do), so “Today” lines up with History, Print, Close the day… and Export…. RowMenu doesn’t change.
  • PC and tablet: nothing changes (no ⋯ sheet; their Today button already has no icon).
  • The date row behind the sheet follows F1’s choice (drawn here as today’s row).

Export… (approved D7): Star’s date picker for From and To (F1, v1.018 / v0.207)

What changes

  • From and To become the picker’s field (“Thu, Oct 1, 2026 ⌄”) instead of the browser’s date box (“10/01/2026” with a small icon). This works with the shared picker as it is — no question of how it opens here.
  • The gray weekday line under each box (“Thursday”, v0.207) goes: the field already starts with the weekday. PROPOSAL — to confirm.
  • No future days (gray), as the Daily report. Wording to OK: the calendar’s gray line “Days after today can’t be chosen.” — the same line as the Daily report, one OK for both.
  • To’s calendar does not gray the days before From: today’s error line under To (“To must be on or after From.”, unchanged) still handles it, so the shared picker needs no change. Its min could do it later if you want.
  • Phones: at 390 wide From and To stay side by side; at 320 wide they stack (as today’s boxes do in the same row). The school line, the count line, Cancel and Download CSV don’t change.

Sample: Worcester, this month so far (Thu Oct 1 – Wed Oct 28, 2026).

History (approved D5): “← Back to the day” as a text link above the heading (F3, v1.020)

What changes

  • Today: an outline button “← Back to the day” beside the “History” heading on PC and tablet, and a bare ← arrow on phones.
  • After, on every size: the back link every other section uses (rule v0.59; drawn with Testing’s BackToTesting look, link-button tc-back: 24 px tall, a 44 px tap area on touch) — a blue text link with a 16 px arrow, above the “History” heading. The heading and month arrows move down one line; the amber “not closed” line and the list don’t change.
  • Same words as today (“Back to the day”), so a screen reader hears the same name on every size (phones now get the words too).

A question for the build: where does the link’s style live?

  • A · Copy the .tc-back look into Finance’s CSS (finance.css). + Finance can build it now; no shared file touched. − A third copy of the same few lines (Testing’s .tc-back, Color Belt’s / Camps’ .ev-back); a later change to the back link has to be made in each.
  • B · Move the back-link style into the shared stylesheet (src/styles/shared.css, Dashboard core’s; not on this branch yet) and use it here. + One back link everywhere, as rule v0.59 intends; Forms’ N8 needs the same thing. − A shared change: it goes through you and the Dashboard core session first, so F3 waits for it.
  • Recommended: B, done once for Finance and Forms (N8) together; if that would hold F3 up, A now and switch to the shared style when it exists.
